title: DEX code loaded at runtime
exploit_reason: Exploitable when an attacker can replace the loaded file or intercept its download
example: val loader = DexClassLoader(dexPath, optDir, null, classLoader)
cause: The app loads DEX code at runtime with DexClassLoader or InMemoryDexClassLoader.
description: Code loaded from storage or the network can be swapped by an attacker, which gives code execution inside the app.
remediation: Ship the code in the APK or use Play Feature Delivery; if loading is unavoidable, keep the file in internal storage, make it read-only and verify its signature first.

title: Native library loaded from a file path
exploit_reason: Exploitable when an attacker can replace the library file
cause: System.load() loads a native library from an absolute path instead of the APK's lib folder.
description: A replaced .so file runs native code with the app's permissions.
remediation: Use System.loadLibrary() with libraries packaged in the APK.

title: Code loaded from another app's package
exploit_reason: Exploitable when a malicious app is installed under the trusted package name
cause: createPackageContext() is called with CONTEXT_INCLUDE_CODE to run another app's classes.
description: If that package is replaced by a malicious app with the same name, its code runs inside this app.
remediation: Do not load code from other packages; if you must, verify the package signature first.

title: SQL query built from concatenated input
exploit_reason: Exploitable when the concatenated value comes from user input or another app
example: db.rawQuery("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'", null);
cause: rawQuery() or execSQL() receives a query string built with + or a Kotlin string template.
description: Input placed in the query can change it (SQL injection) and read or modify other rows.
remediation: Use ? placeholders with selectionArgs, or Room/SQLiteDatabase.query() with bound arguments.

title: Zip entry name used as a file path (Zip Slip)
exploit_reason: Exploitable when the app unpacks an archive an attacker can supply
example: ZipEntry entry = zis.getNextEntry(); File out = new File(destDir, entry.getName());
cause: A ZipEntry's name is joined to a directory to build the output file path.
description: Entry names like ../../shared_prefs/x.xml write outside the target folder and can overwrite app files.
remediation: Resolve the canonical path and reject entries that do not start with the canonical target directory.

title: File path built from a content URI (path traversal)
exploit_reason: Any app that can query the provider controls the URI
example: public ParcelFileDescriptor openFile(Uri uri, String mode) { File f = new File(dir, uri.getLastPathSegment());
cause: openFile() builds a file path from the URI's last path segment.
description: An encoded ../ in the URI lets other apps read or write files outside the shared folder.
remediation: Canonicalize the path and check it stays inside the shared directory, or use FileProvider.

title: XML parser processes DOCTYPE declarations (XXE)
exploit_reason: Exploitable when the parsed XML comes from the network or another app
cause: DOCTYPE processing is switched on for an XML parser.
description: External entities in untrusted XML can read local files or trigger requests (XXE).
remediation: Leave DOCTYPE processing off (the default) or set disallow-doctype-decl to true.

title: Java deserialization of a stream
exploit_reason: Exploitable when the stream carries data from outside the app
cause: Objects are read with ObjectInputStream.
description: Deserializing attacker data can instantiate unexpected classes and run gadget chains.
remediation: Use a data format such as JSON or Protocol Buffers; if you must deserialize, allow-list the classes.

title: Shell command executed
exploit_reason: Exploitable when part of the command comes from input
cause: The app runs a shell command built from a variable with Runtime.exec() or ProcessBuilder.
description: Input placed in the command can add extra commands (OS command injection).
remediation: Avoid shell commands; use Android APIs, or pass a fixed command with separate, validated arguments.

title: WebView loads a URL from an Intent
exploit_reason: Any app that can start this component chooses the page the WebView opens
cause: loadUrl() is called with a value taken straight from the incoming Intent.
description: Other apps can open javascript: or file:// URLs in the app's WebView (cross-app scripting).
remediation: Allow-list schemes and hosts before loading, and keep JavaScript and file access off for external URLs.

title: WebView saves passwords
exploit_reason: Needs access to the app's private data
cause: WebSettings.setSavePassword(true) is called.
description: Passwords typed into the WebView are stored in plain text in the WebView database.
remediation: Remove the call; it is deprecated and saving passwords is off by default.

title: Intent received from another app is started (intent redirection)
exploit_reason: Any app that can reach this component chooses which Intent is started
cause: An Intent taken from the incoming Intent's extras is passed to startActivity().
description: Other apps can make the app open its own non-exported components or grant URI permissions.
remediation: Validate the nested Intent (component, flags) or use a PendingIntent created by the trusted sender.

title: Mutable PendingIntent
exploit_reason: Exploitable when the PendingIntent wraps an implicit Intent and is handed to another app
cause: A PendingIntent is created with FLAG_MUTABLE.
description: The receiving app can fill in the empty fields of the Intent and act with this app's identity.
remediation: Use FLAG_IMMUTABLE unless mutability is required, and always set an explicit component.

title: Sticky broadcast sent
exploit_reason: Any app can read or remove sticky broadcasts without a permission
cause: sendStickyBroadcast() is used.
description: Sticky broadcasts cannot be protected by permissions: any app can read the data or remove the broadcast.
remediation: Use a regular broadcast with a permission, or another IPC mechanism.

title: Receiver registered as exported at runtime
exploit_reason: Any app can send broadcasts to it
cause: registerReceiver() is called with RECEIVER_EXPORTED.
description: Other apps can send forged broadcasts to the receiver.
remediation: Use RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED unless other apps must reach it, and validate every broadcast.

title: Task reparenting allowed (StrandHogg)
exploit_reason: Needs a malicious app on the device
cause: An activity sets android:allowTaskReparenting="true".
description: A malicious app can move the activity into its task and show fake screens in its place (task hijacking).
remediation: Remove allowTaskReparenting and set an empty taskAffinity on sensitive activities.

title: App is debuggable
exploit_reason: Needs USB or adb access to the device
cause: The manifest sets android:debuggable="true".
description: Anyone with adb can attach a debugger, run code as the app and read its private data.
remediation: Remove the attribute; Gradle sets it only for debug builds.

title: SecureRandom with a fixed or weak seed
exploit_reason: The attacker needs to know or guess the seed
cause: SecureRandom is seeded by the app or uses the SHA1PRNG provider.
description: A seeded generator can produce predictable keys, tokens or IVs.
remediation: Use new SecureRandom() without a seed and let the platform seed it.

title: Non-cryptographic random for a security value
exploit_reason: The attacker needs enough outputs to predict the next value
cause: java.util.Random is used in a file that handles OTPs.
description: java.util.Random is predictable, so codes or tokens made with it can be guessed.
remediation: Use SecureRandom for any security-relevant value.

title: Asymmetric key shorter than 2048 bits
exploit_reason: The attacker first needs data protected by the key
cause: KeyPairGenerator is initialized with a 512, 768 or 1024 bit key.
description: Keys this short can be factored or brute-forced with modern hardware.
remediation: Use at least 2048-bit RSA (3072 for long-term data) or EC P-256.

title: Download saved to public external storage
exploit_reason: Apps with storage access (and the user) can read or replace the file
cause: DownloadManager saves a file to a public external directory.
description: Other apps can read the file or replace it before the app opens it.
remediation: Download into app-specific storage and verify the file before use.

title: Sensitive value copied to the clipboard
exploit_reason: Keyboards and other apps with clipboard access can read it
cause: A password, token, OTP or card value is put on the clipboard.
description: Clipboard contents can be read by other apps and keyboards and are shown in clipboard history.
remediation: Avoid copying secrets; if needed, mark the clip sensitive (ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE).
